title: Concorde at Filton
text: The first British-built Concorde flew from Filton to RAF Fairford on 9 April 1969, piloted by Brian Trubshaw. Concorde was 61.66 m long with a 25.6 m wingspan, and cruised at up to Mach 2.04; its nose drooped 5° for take-off and 12.5° for landing. Concorde's last-ever flight, on 26 November 2003, ended here.

title: Concorde 216, G-BOAF
text: Several of Filton's hangars reopened in 2017 as the Aerospace Bristol museum, with a purpose-built hangar for Concorde G-BOAF.
check: That G-BOAF made the final flight in 2003 is general knowledge; Wikipedia's pages fetched here confirm only the date and destination.

title: Filton airfield
text: Sir George White set up the British and Colonial Aeroplane Company here in 1910 (the Bristol Aeroplane Company from 1920). The runway, 2,467 m long and 91 m wide, was extended for the Brabazon's first flight in 1949. The airfield closed for business at the end of 2012; the new district of Brabazon is being built on it.

title: The Brabazon hangar
text: Built in the late 1940s to assemble the giant Bristol Brabazon airliner; its doors were among the largest in the world.

title: 25 September 1940
text: German aircraft raided Filton, causing extensive damage to the aircraft factories; several air-raid shelters were hit, with heavy loss of life.
